thesis_summary: Copper at $13,202/t is substantially a US Section 232 tariff-expectations premium layered on top of a structural electrification bid; the underlying 2026 refined balance is a surplus (~96,000 t ICSG forecast), speculative longs are at a COT Index of ~96/100 with ETF flows already reversing, and the curve is in contango imposing ~5-6% annualised roll drag — the risk/reward for a fresh long is negative-skewed until the tariff binary resolves and crowded positioning normalises.
key_risks: US Section 232 refined copper tariff deferral or rejection strips $1,000-1,500/t from LME price
Crowded-long unwind (COT Index ~96/100, ~66,500 net contracts) amplifies any bearish catalyst into a self-reinforcing selloff
COMEX 652,000 t inventory overhang creates a 12-18 month US demand air-pocket if tariff is shelved
DXY near 15-month highs (~101.3-101.6) and 10-year TIPS at 2.16% are active macro headwinds
Chinese smelter-cut compliance unverified from official sources — if cuts fail, refined surplus persists and concentrate tightness (zero TC/RCs) overstates tightening risk
Contango curve: ~5-6% annualised roll drag on a long position requires material price appreciation just to break even
relative_view: Copper is not the most attractive commodity in the tracked set for a fresh long today — gold has a cleaner macro setup without the tariff binary risk or crowded-long overhang and carries near-zero roll drag; aluminium warrants a comparative setup run as the closest base-metal alternative
